info.title: ResourcePack AI API
info.description:
Create packs, generate blocks, models, items, GUIs, icons and sounds into them, and download the result.

Every generation is asynchronous: the endpoint answers 202 with a job handle and you poll it. Calls spend the same AI Credits the app does.

bearerAuth.description: Your API key, from the account page. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer rpai_…`.

Error.description: Every failure from this API has this shape.

file_fetch_failed.description: A file given by `url` couldn't be downloaded.

not_a_pack.description: An import's file isn't a resource pack, or holds nothing a pack here can use. `message` says which.

invalid_api_key.description: The key isn't one of ours, or it has been revoked.

wrong_key_kind.description: An MCP key sent to the REST API, or an API key sent to the MCP server. Each only opens its own.

insufficient_credits.description: Not enough AI Credits to run this. Nothing was started or charged.

plan_required.description: The key is valid, but its account's plan does not include the API.

account_suspended.description: The account is suspended, so its keys open nothing. `message` says until when, if the suspension has an end date.

forbidden.description: Valid key, but not permitted to do this in this pack.

pack_limit_reached.description: The account is at its plan's pack limit.

asset_limit_reached.description: The pack is at its asset limit.

not_found.description: No such pack, asset or job.

upload_not_found.description: No upload by that id. Uploads expire after fifteen minutes and are used once.

conflict.description: That vanilla target is already reskinned in this pack. Change it in the Studio rather than overwriting it.

already_running.description: An AI edit or generation of that asset is still running. Wait for its job, then send the edit again.

still_generating.description: The asset exists but isn't finished. Poll its job until it's ready.

not_linked.description: Nobody is linked to receive a push: your code for this pack (`GET /packs/{pack}/link`) has not been claimed with `/rp sync`, and you are not on the test server with `/permlink`.

not_a_vehicle.description: The model is not a vehicle yet. Make it one with `POST /packs/{pack}/vehicles/{model}`.

generation_failed.description: That asset's generation failed. Its job carries the reason.

no_file.description: That asset has nothing in the `format` asked for: a 2D shader overlay and an emote have no picture on the server, and only a VFX and a text effect have an animation. `message` says what there is.

file_too_large.description: The file is over the limit for what it's being used as. `message` says the limit.

rate_limited.description: Too many requests. `message` says how long to wait; see Rate limits.

unavailable.description: The feature behind this endpoint is switched off.

server_limit_reached.description: The pack is bound to as many servers as it may, claim codes still waiting included. Unbind one first.

skin_limit_reached.description: The account holds as many skins as it may. Delete one first.

push_failed.description: The pack was built but the server holding the player could not be reached, or refused it. `message` says which.

distribution_cap.description: The account (or team) has served its plan's players for this month, so a new release cannot be published. Players still get the live one.

no_such_player.description: No resourcepack.ai account has verified that Minecraft username. Invite them by email instead.

too_many_invites.description: The pack has as many invitations waiting as it may. Withdraw one first.

nothing_to_export.description: The pack holds nothing that export format is built from yet, or all of it is still generating. `message` says which.

request_failed.description: Something went wrong that doesn't have a more specific code.

get.description:
Page until `nextCursor` is null. An asset's `id` is also its job handle, so this is how you find the handle for something generated in an earlier run.

Every asset says what it is in `type` — `block`, `item`, `item3d`, `gui`, `hud`, `dialog`, `icon`, `sound` and so on — and that is the field to filter and branch on. `kind` is the file format it is stored as (`texture`, `model`, `font`, `sound`), which several types share: a block, an item sprite, a GUI, a HUD and a dialog are all `texture`s. Some types are parts of another asset rather than assets of their own (`block_face`, `model_texture`, `item_model`).

**Shaders, text effects, VFX, emotes and emote groups are listed too**, after everything else, with `kind` set to the store they live in (`shader`, `vfx`, `emote`, `emote_group`) because they are documents rather than stored files: download one as JSON or as a picture with `GET /packs/{pack}/assets/{kind}/{name}` and its `format`. Their `name` is the id to send to `POST /packs/{pack}/assets/{kind}/{name}/edit`, and their `id` is a job handle like any other. The cursor pages across both parts as one list, so keep passing `nextCursor` until it is null.

post.description:
Puts a file you already have into the pack — the Studio's Upload button. Free: nothing is generated, though it counts toward the pack's asset limit.

What `file` must be, and what else each `type` needs:

- `block` — a PNG. `target` is the vanilla block texture it replaces (`stone_bricks`); without one it is a texture of your own, named `name`. Square, 1–256px, or send `size` to resample. `faceSlot` with a `target` replaces one face only.
- `item` — a PNG. `target` is the vanilla item it replaces (`diamond_sword`); without one it is a custom item named `name`. Square, 8–256px, or send `size`.
- `icon` — a PNG of any shape, drawn as a chat glyph. Needs `name`. Kept at its own size when 32px tall or less, else 16 tall; `height` overrides it (1–256).
- `model` — Minecraft block model JSON, or a Blockbench `.bbmodel` (its embedded textures come in with it).
- `sound` — Ogg Vorbis, or WAV (converted to Ogg). Needs `event`. MP3 is not accepted; convert it first.
- `gui` — a 256x256 PNG sheet. `target` is the vanilla screen it reskins (`generic_54`, `furnace`…).
- `hud` — a PNG of the HUD sheet, at its own size.
- `armor` — a PNG armour sheet (64x32). `target` is the vanilla set (`iron`, `diamond`…).
- `armor3d` — a Blockbench `.bbmodel` of a 3D armour set.

Images must be PNG. Answers 201 with the asset ready — there is no job to wait for.

get.description:
The asset's own bytes, with the matching content type: PNG for textures and icons, JSON for models, Ogg Vorbis for sounds.

The path takes an asset's `kind` and `name` exactly as the asset listing reports them — `texture/item:rusted_key` for an item sprite, `texture/gui:shop_menu` for a GUI, `vfx/frost_burst` for a VFX — so copy both from there rather than building them from its type.

A shader, text effect, VFX, emote or emote group is a document rather than stored bytes, and `format` says how to have it. `file` (the default) is that document as JSON: a VFX's recipe (what its page's **Download recipe** saves), a shader object, an emote's keyframes, an emote group's parts. `picture` is a PNG drawn on the server: a VFX as six moments across its timeline, left to right, and a 3D shader object or a text effect as its card. `animation` is a GIF of a VFX or a text effect playing. A 2D shader overlay and an emote have no picture on the server (the browser draws them) and answer `no_file` for one. A stored asset always answers its own file, whatever `format` says.

Asking before it's ready answers 409 rather than handing back the placeholder that sits there while it generates — a blank PNG that looked like a result is the one genuinely misleading answer available here.

post.description:
What the Studio's **Sync** button does: builds the pack and sends it straight to a player in game, who gets it without rejoining. It reaches the key owner: their account if it is linked with `/permlink` and they are on the test server, otherwise whoever claimed your code for this pack (`GET /packs/{pack}/link`) with `/rp sync` on a server running RP Engine. Anybody else is out of reach on purpose.

When nothing has changed since the last push to the same person in this session, nothing is built and `status` is `unchanged`; send `force: true` to push anyway. Free.

Emotes are pushed with the default player model rather than each player's own skin, which only the Studio can fetch. Press Sync in the Studio for skinned emotes.

post.description:
What an asset's **Give in game** button does, for whoever is linked to receive a push (see `POST /packs/{pack}/push`): a model, block or item lands in their hands, a GUI or dialog opens, an icon or text effect is said in chat, a sound plays, an armour set is worn, a VFX is cast and a 3D shader object is placed in front of them. The command is built from the pack, never sent: you name the asset, by the `kind` and `name` the asset listing reports (`shader/<id>` and `vfx/<id>` for those two).

The pack itself has to be on their client for most of these to look right, so push it first. Free.

Changes the fields you send and keeps the rest. **Choosing a take** is `{"take": "2"}` sent on its own: that take becomes the audio the pack ships, instantly and for free, and the others stay to choose between. Its label is changed with `POST /packs/{pack}/assets/sound/{sound}/rename`.

An `event` that names a vanilla sound (`entity.creeper.primed`) replaces it in game; any other (`custom.laser`) is a new one `/playsound` and RP Engine's `/rp sound` can play.

get.description:
A handle looks like `<pack>:<kind>:<name>` and comes back from every generation endpoint. A pack import's is `<pack>:import`, and its answer carries `import` (what came in, what didn't and why) where a generation's carries `asset`.

Shaders, VFX and emotes keep stores of their own, and an AI edit is a run on an asset that already exists, so their handles name that instead of a file format (`<pack>:shader:<id>`, `<pack>:vfx:<id>`, `<pack>:emote:<id>`, `<pack>:emote_group:<id>`, `<pack>:edit:<key>`) and their answers carry no `asset`. An edit's job reads `ready` once the edit has been saved.

A skin has no pack, so its handle is `skin:<id>`, its `pack` is null and its answer carries `skin`.

There's no jobs table behind this: generation is two-phase, so the asset row is written up front with status `generating` and the runner fills it in. The asset *is* the job record, which is why a handle stays resolvable long after the run finished.

Polling always terminates. A run that dies without recording anything reads as `error` once it passes the stale cutoff.

post.description:
Changes an asset that already exists from a sentence (`make it rustier`, `slower`, `add a second ring`), exactly as the Studio's **Edit with AI** button does, and at the same price. The asset is changed in place.

**Which assets.** A stored asset is addressed by the `kind` and `name` the asset listing reports, as for a download: a `block` (`texture/mossy_bricks`), an `item` sprite (`texture/item:rusted_key`), a `model`, `item3d` or `vehicle` (`model/lantern`) and an `icon` (`font/heart`). The rest are addressed by their own kind and the `id` their generation returned: a 3D shader object or a text effect (`shader/<id>`), a VFX (`vfx/<id>`) and an emote (`emote/<id>`). A `hud`, a chest `gui` and a 2D `armor` set (`texture/hud:<id>`, `texture/gui:<id>`, `texture/armor:<set>`) are redrawn whole by their generator with the change as its brief, so they take minutes and cost what a generation does. A Dialog-style `dialog` (`texture/gui:<id>`) and a `rank_tag` (`font/<id>`) are changed while you wait and saved before this answers, so their job is already `ready`. Sounds, 3D armour and HUD shaders are changed in the Studio, and are refused here.

**Modes.** `mode` picks which of the asset's AI buttons this is. `edit` (the default) is Edit with AI. `animate` is a model's **Animate with AI**: it writes or changes the model's bones and animations from a description of the motion (`the lid creaks open and shut`); set `addParts` to let it add the cubes the motion needs, and `fromAnimation` to start where one of its animations ends. An emote's edit already is its Animate with AI, so either word works there. `restyle` is a dialog's **Restyle with AI**: a new look for one page (colours, kit, banner) with nothing moved, reworded or rewired. On a dialog, `page` says which page (the first by default) and `scope` whether to rewrite only the part that changes per page (`part`, the default when the page has one) or the whole page.

**Limits.** An emote's instruction is up to 500 characters, a VFX's or a text effect's 600, a 3D object's 800. One edit at a time per asset: a second while the first runs answers `already_running`.

The `job` polls like a generation's. When it is `ready`, the asset holds the change: download it again to see it.

post.summary: Check whether content was generated here
post.description:
For marketplaces: check whether files uploaded to you were generated by ResourcePack AI. No API key.

Send up to 256 hashes per call. Each returns a result in the order you sent it, so you can pair answers to files without matching on the hash yourself.

`generated` is definitive. **`no_record` is not a negative** — it means only that the content is not in our registry, never that a human made it.

[The Origin check guide](/api-reference/origin) has how to compute the hash, which you must follow exactly or every lookup misses silently.

Rate limited to 60 requests a minute per address, since there is no key to count instead.

The same registry, queried k-anonymously — for a marketplace that would rather not send us the content hashes of what its users upload.

Send the first 5 characters of a hash, get back every fingerprint we hold that starts with them, and match the rest locally.

Hashes are computed exactly as for the lookup endpoint, and the same caveat applies: a hit is definitive, a miss is not a negative. See [the Origin check guide](/api-reference/origin).
